mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower (p > 0.05) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months compared to non-tightening periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months indicates weakening labor market conditions, reducing consumer demand and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals deteriorating aggregate demand, which compresses corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation between GDPC1 YoY decline and S&P 500 60-day forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces output, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during four-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decrease in CPIAUCSL (core inflation) over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over two months
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation between the joint FEDFUNDS rise and CPIAUCSL fall and subsequent 20-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its trend by more than 1% in a single month, combined with a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a late-cycle labor market overheating, which precedes equity market corrections and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > trend +1% and UNRATE falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative following such joint labor market signals.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation between six-month HOUST above MA and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening aggregate demand, which expands corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both rise for three consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation between joint GDPC1 and RSAFS rises and subsequent 20-day S&P 500 returns.
